# Validating Lomb-Scargle Results in R

First lets load in our data and grab out one individual to start just to see how lsp works

```{r}
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(lomb)
library(ggplot2)
```

```{r}

# 1. Import the dataset
csv_path = "../../GenerateActivityBins/diet_1min_activity_downsample_rollingMean.csv"
df = read_csv(csv_path)

# Isolate a single rhythmic individual for the cross-check
# Update the treatment/replicate/individual to match one you want to verify
target_ind = df %>% 
  filter(treatment == "DD-diet", replicate == "rep1", individual == 1) #%>%
  #arrange(ZT_continuous)
```

```{r}
# quick plot of this individuals activity


# Create a dataframe for the dark phase (night) shading
# Starts at ZT 16, ends at ZT 24, repeating every 24 hours up to ~100h
night_bars <- data.frame(
  xmin = seq(16, 100, by = 24),
  xmax = seq(24, 108, by = 24)
)

# QC Plot: Raw activity profile over the entire 96-hour experiment
qc_plot <- ggplot(target_ind, aes(x = ZT_continuous, y = filtered_distance / 281)) +
  # 1. Add the gray background bars FIRST so they sit behind the data
  geom_rect(data = night_bars, inherit.aes = FALSE,
            aes(xmin = xmin, xmax = xmax, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf),
            fill = "grey40", alpha = 0.25) +
            
  # 2. Add the activity data on top
  geom_area(fill = "dodgerblue4", alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_line(color = "dodgerblue4", linewidth = 0.5) +
  
  theme_classic() +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 100, by = 12), expand = c(0, 0)) +
  labs(
    title = "QC: Continuous Activity Profile (Rep 1, Ind 1)",
    x = "Zeitgeber Time (Hours)",
    y = "Filtered Distance"
  ) +
  theme(
    axis.text = element_text(color = "black", size = 10, face = "bold"),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 11, face = "bold"),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold")
  )

print(qc_plot)
```

```{r}
# The lomb::lsp function accepts a 2-column dataframe: [Time, Observation]
ls_data = target_ind %>% select(ZT_continuous, filtered_distance)

# Run the periodogram bounded between 20 and 28 hours
# alpha = 0.05 automatically calculates and draws the FAP threshold line
ls_result = lsp(ls_data, 
                 from = 2, 
                 to = 96, 
                 type = "period", 
                 alpha = 0.05, 
                 plot = F,
                 main = "R lomb::lsp() Verification (20-28h)",
                 ofac = 50)



# 2. Extract the math into a clean dataframe
periodogram_df = data.frame(
  Period = ls_result$scanned,
  Power = ls_result$power
)

# Extract the FAP threshold (the red dashed line)
fap_threshold <- ls_result$sig.level

# Print exact statistical outputs to compare with Python
cat("Peak Period (h):", ls_result$peak.at[1], "\n")
cat("Peak Power:", ls_result$peak, "\n")
cat("p-value:", ls_result$p.value, "\n")

# 3. Plot manually using ggplot2
ggplot(periodogram_df, aes(x = Period, y = Power)) +
  geom_line(color = "black", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = fap_threshold, color = "red", linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 1) +
  # Add a gold star at the peak
  annotate("point", x = ls_result$peak.at[1], y = ls_result$peak, 
           color = "gold", size = 5, shape = 21, fill = "gold", stroke = 1) +
  annotate("text", x = ls_result$peak.at[1] + 0.3, y = ls_result$peak, 
           label = paste0(round(ls_result$peak.at[1], 1), "h"), fontface = "bold") +
  theme_classic() +
  labs(
    title = paste("R Lomb-Scargle Verification: Rep 1, Ind 1"),
    x = "Period (Hours)",
    y = "Scargle Power"
  ) +
  # Lock the x-axis to exactly 20-28h so it visually matches your Python plots
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, 96)) +
  theme(
    axis.text = element_text(color = "black", size = 11, face = "bold"),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 13, face = "bold"),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold")
  )

```

# Scaling to All Individuals

```{r}
# 4. Define function to extract rhythmicity stats and calculate Acrophase
extract_rhythm_stats <- function(df_subset, keys) {
  ls_data <- df_subset %>% select(ZT_continuous, filtered_distance)
  
  # Run high-resolution LSP
  ls_result <- lsp(ls_data, from = 16, to = 32, type = "period", 
                   ofac = 50, alpha = 0.05, plot = FALSE)
  
  peak_period <- ls_result$peak.at[1]
  peak_power <- ls_result$peak
  fap_threshold <- ls_result$sig.level
  
  # Evaluate significance
  is_rhythmic <- peak_power >= fap_threshold
  
  acrophase_zt <- NA
  active_phase <- NA
  
  # If rhythmic, use Harmonic Regression (Cosinor) to find the acrophase
  if (is_rhythmic) {
    t <- ls_data$ZT_continuous
    y <- ls_data$filtered_distance
    
    # Fit cosine and sine waves fixed at the winning period
    cos_term <- cos(2 * pi * t / peak_period)
    sin_term <- sin(2 * pi * t / peak_period)
    fit <- lm(y ~ cos_term + sin_term)
    
    # Extract coefficients
    beta1 <- coef(fit)["cos_term"]
    beta2 <- coef(fit)["sin_term"]
    
    # Calculate phase angle in radians and ensure it is positive
    phase_rad <- atan2(beta2, beta1)
    if (phase_rad < 0) {
      phase_rad <- phase_rad + 2 * pi
    }
    
    # Convert radians to hours relative to t=0, then map to 24h ZT scale
    acrophase_hours <- phase_rad * (peak_period / (2 * pi))
    acrophase_zt <- acrophase_hours %% 24
    
    # Categorize peak timing (Day = ZT 0-16, Night = ZT 16-24)
    active_phase <- ifelse(acrophase_zt < 16, "Day", "Night")
  }
  
  # Return a clean 1-row summary for this individual
  data.frame(
    Peak_Period = peak_period,
    Peak_Power = peak_power,
    FAP_Threshold = fap_threshold,
    Is_Rhythmic = is_rhythmic,
    Acrophase_ZT = acrophase_zt,
    Peak_Activity_Window = active_phase
  )
}

cat("Extracting significant periods and mapping acrophases...\n")

# 5. Apply across the full dataset
rhythm_summary_df <- df %>%
  group_by(treatment, replicate, individual) %>%
  filter((max(ZT_continuous) - min(ZT_continuous)) >= 48.0) %>%
  group_modify(~ extract_rhythm_stats(.x, .y)) %>%
  ungroup()

# View the extracted data
head(rhythm_summary_df)

# 6. Isolate just the peak stats so we don't overplot stars/text 1000 times per facet
peak_stats <- all_lomb_data %>%
  distinct(treatment, replicate, individual, Peak_Period, Peak_Power, FAP_Threshold)

cat("Done! Successfully extracted periodograms for", nrow(peak_stats), "individuals.\n")
```

```{r}
# 7. Generate the Faceted Matrix Plot in ggplot2

# Define the exact colors used in your Python script
treat_colors <- c("LD-diet" = "#EE99AA", "DD-diet" = "#994455")

ggplot(all_lomb_data, aes(x = Period, y = Power)) +
  # Main periodogram curve colored by treatment
  geom_line(aes(color = treatment), linewidth = 0.8) +
  
  # The FAP p=0.05 threshold dashed line
  geom_hline(data = peak_stats, aes(yintercept = FAP_Threshold), 
             color = "red", linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.6, alpha = 0.8) +
  
  # The peak marker (using a filled circle with a white outline to match Python)
  geom_point(data = peak_stats, aes(x = Peak_Period, y = Peak_Power, fill = treatment), 
             shape = 21, size = 3, color = "white", stroke = 0.5) +
  
  # The peak period text label (hjust = 0 keeps it from overlapping the dot)
  geom_text(data = peak_stats, aes(x = Peak_Period + 0.3, y = Peak_Power + 0.002, 
                                   label = paste0(round(Peak_Period, 1), "h"), 
                                   color = treatment), 
            size = 3.5, fontface = "bold", hjust = 0) +
  
  # Create the matrix grid: Rows = Replicates, Columns = Individuals
  facet_grid(replicate ~ individual) +
  
  # Formatting constraints
  scale_color_manual(values = treat_colors) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = treat_colors) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(14, 34)) + # Lock visual window to target circadian range
  theme_bw() +
  labs(
    #title = "R Lomb-Scargle Matrix (20-28h Search Window)",
    x = "Period (Hours)",
    y = "Scargle Power"
  ) +
  theme(
    strip.background = element_rect(fill = "grey90", color = "black"),
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 11),
    axis.text = element_text(color = "black"),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "top",
    legend.title = element_blank()
  )

```



```{r}
#Filter the summary dataframe to only include significant rhythms
rhythmic_only <- rhythm_summary_df %>% filter(Is_Rhythmic == TRUE)

#Define exact colors
treat_colors <- c("LD-diet" = "#EE99AA", "DD-diet" = "#994455")

#1. Acrophase Boxplot
acrophase_box <- ggplot(rhythmic_only, aes(x = treatment, y = Acrophase_ZT)) +

#Add the gray background bar for the night phase (ZT 16-24) on the y-axis
annotate("rect", ymin = 16, ymax = 24, xmin = -Inf, xmax = Inf,
fill = "grey40", alpha = 0.2) +

#Add jittered points in the background
geom_jitter(width = 0.15, alpha = 0.3, size = 2, color = "black") +

#Add boxplots on top
geom_boxplot(aes(fill = treatment), width = 0.4, alpha = 0.8,
outlier.shape = NA, linewidth = 0.8, color = "black") +
scale_fill_manual(values = treat_colors) +
scale_x_discrete(labels = c("LD-diet" = "LD", "DD-diet" = "DD")) +
scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 24, by = 4), limits = c(0, 24), expand = c(0, 0)) +
theme_classic() +
labs(
title = "Acrophase of Significant Rhythms",
x = "Treatment",
y = "Acrophase (ZT Hours)"
) +
theme(
axis.text = element_text(color = "black", size = 11, face = "bold"),
axis.title = element_text(size = 13, face = "bold"),
plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
legend.position = "none" # Hide legend since x-axis has the labels
)

print(acrophase_box)

#2. Peak Period Boxplot
period_box <- ggplot(rhythmic_only, aes(x = treatment, y = Peak_Period)) +

#Add jittered points in the background
geom_jitter(width = 0.15, alpha = 0.3, size = 2, color = "black") +

#Add boxplots on top
geom_boxplot(aes(fill = treatment), width = 0.4, alpha = 0.8,
outlier.shape = NA, linewidth = 0.8, color = "black") +
scale_fill_manual(values = treat_colors) +
scale_x_discrete(labels = c("LD-diet" = "LD", "DD-diet" = "DD")) +
scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(16, 32, by = 2), limits = c(15.5, 32.5), expand = c(0, 0)) +
theme_classic() +
labs(
title = "Circadian Period of Significant Rhythms",
x = "Treatment",
y = "Peak Period (Hours)"
) +
theme(
axis.text = element_text(color = "black", size = 11, face = "bold"),
axis.title = element_text(size = 13, face = "bold"),
plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
legend.position = "none" # Hide legend since x-axis has the labels
)

print(period_box)
```
